title: Higgs Fluctuation Solver in Four Dimensions: Part I-A Matrix-Free Global-Scalar Bounce and Determinant-Renormalization Audit
summary: We report a matrix-free numerical pipeline for semiclassical false-vacuum decay in a four-component global-O(4) scalar theory in four Euclidean dimensions. The calculation combines continuum bounce shooting, action relaxation, channel-resolved fluctuation spectra, deflated stochastic Lanczos quadrature (SLQ), and a continuum partial-wave determinant with Gel'fand-Yaglom radial ratios and large-angular-momentum subtraction. For the benchmark potential, the bounce action is B = 145.203947 and the tail residual is 0.281955%. On an L = 26, h = 0.8 lattice, the relaxed field achieves an RMS EOM residual of 4.43 x 10^-12; its low spectrum contains one negative radial mode, four lattice translations, and three near-zero internal modes. The 16-probe bare SLQ trace-log is -2079.9042 +/- 6.4504. Under the subtraction prescription, the scalar partial-wave calculation returns a primed trace-log of 40.9324 at mu = mF = sqrt(0.4), giving a determinant factor of 1.2931 x 10^-9. We show the leading rho^8 potential is not closed under its scalar one-loop divergence: local rho^10 and rho^12 counterterms are required, leaving finite coefficients unmatched; hence this is a prescription-level result, not a complete EFT prediction. The translation-normalized scalar expression is 5.9974 x 10^-70 in lattice energy units to the fourth power, omitting the internal-orientation Jacobian. We summarize tested SU(2) operator and pole-algebra infrastructure, identifying finite full-gauge matching and controlled limits as open work.

title: Spontaneous chiral-symmetry breaking in four-dimensional QCD with $A_x=A_y=0$ projection in dimensional reduction gauge
summary: We investigate spontaneous chiral-symmetry breaking in four-dimensional (4D) QCD in the dimensional reduction (DR) gauge, defined so as to minimize $R_{\mathrm{DR}}\equiv~\int d^{4}s ~ \mathrm{Tr} \left[ A_{x}^{2}(s) + A_{y}^{2}(s) \right]$. We consider ``$tz$-projection" of $A_{x,y}(s) \to 0$ and ``$xy$-projection" of $A_{t,z}(s) \to 0$, respectively, for the gauge configuration generated in the DR gauge, in a similar sense to Abelian, monopole and photon projections in the maximally Abelian gauge. The chiral condensate is estimated from the low-lying Dirac-eigenvalue density $ρ(λ)$ using the Banks-Casher relation. By the $tz$-projection in the DR gauge, the chiral condensate is largely reserved. In contrast, the chiral condensate becomes zero by the $xy$-projection in the DR gauge. This indicates that $A_{t}(s)$ and $A_{z}(s)$ play a dominant role, while $A_{x}(s)$ and $A_{y}(s)$ play no role, in spontaneous chiral-symmetry breaking in the DR gauge.

title: Learning Low Modes of the Wilson Dirac Operator with Gauge-Equivariant Networks
comment: 9 pages, 4 figures, 1 table. Proceedings of the 43rd International Symposium on Lattice Field Theory (Lattice 2026), 26 July - 1 August 2026, University of Maryland, College Park, USA
summary: In adaptive multigrid, test vectors that better approximate the low-mode subspace of the Wilson Dirac operator $D$ can reduce the solve time, but their construction can be costly. In some cases, the setup takes longer than a single solve. To reduce the cost of generating test vectors, we train networks built from gauge-equivariant parallel-transport layers once on a quenched ensemble, using a Rayleigh-Ritz loss for $D^\dagger D$. We then test whether the trained networks maintain their performance at other hopping parameters and on configurations not used in training. In these tests, the network outputs are used as test vectors, and the costly $V$-cycle refinement in the adaptive setup is omitted to reduce the setup time. This substantially reduces the setup time while leaving the solve time largely unchanged in most cases. Near the critical hopping parameter $κ_c$, the solve time is also reduced in some cases.

title: Dyon Condensation at $θ=2π$ from Wilson-'t Hooft Loops in Yang-Mills Theory
comment: 8 pages, 5 figures, 2 tables. Talk presented at the 43rd International Symposium on Lattice Field Theory (Lattice2026), July 26 - August 1st, 2026, University of Maryland, College Park, USA
summary: Although Yang--Mills theories at $θ$ and $θ+2π$ are physically equivalent, their periodicity is realized nontrivially in the presence of a background field for the $1$-form center symmetry. The confining vacua at $θ=0$ and $2π$ are therefore expected to have distinct symmetry-protected topological labels. We test this expectation in $SU(2)$ lattice Yang--Mills theory by measuring 't~Hooft and dyonic Wilson--'t~Hooft loops at $θ=2π$. A $1$-form-covariant DBW2 flow makes the global reweighting factor numerically benign while retaining the physical non-integer topological charge in a defect ensemble. The dyonic loop exhibits a clear perimeter-law plateau on two lattice volumes. The direct 't~Hooft-loop signal is noise-limited but has the magnitude and distance dependence expected for an area law. Taken together with the Wilson--'t~Hooft classification, these results provide numerical evidence for the dyonic oblique-confinement pattern at $θ=2π$. This talk is based on our recent paper (arXiv:2606.13428).

title: 2Flow2SN: Dusty Supernova Cosmology with Photometric Redshifts and Contamination using Neural Simulation-Based Inference
comment: 30 pages, 9 figures, 6 tables, submitted to MNRAS
summary: Photometric Type Ia supernova (SN Ia) cosmology in the era of the Vera C. Rubin Observatory's Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) demands statistical frameworks that simultaneously account for selection effects, photometric redshift uncertainties and non-Ia contamination at scale. We present FlowSN2, a modular statistical framework combining hierarchical Bayesian modelling and simulation-based inference (SBI), that reframes photometric SN cosmology from a regression task to a joint inference problem over light curve summaries and photometric redshifts. By employing neural likelihood estimation via normalising flows, FlowSN2 approximates the data distributions of selected objects in a form that can be reused across different cosmological models, achieving amortisation over the Hubble diagram. This amortisation enables inference across alternative cosmological parameterisations, such as $w_0w_a\mathrm{CDM}$, away from the fiducial training cosmology. The framework integrates a standardisation model that disentangles intrinsic SN variations from extrinsic host-galaxy dust effects and adopts a principled Bayesian resampling approach to propagate SN classification uncertainty, without requiring an explicit contaminant likelihood. Across simulated tests spanning five cosmological parameter sets, our framework recovers true cosmological and population parameters, with posteriors in close agreement with both tractable analytical solutions and pure-Ia baselines. Conveniently, the framework enables Bayesian model comparison at negligible additional computational cost, providing a valuable tool for addressing debates surrounding SN standardisation and evolving dark energy. Capable of scaling to over a hundred thousand SNe without retraining, FlowSN2 offers an interpretable and statistically principled solution for cosmological inference with upcoming wide-field photometric surveys.

title: Twisted scattering from Chern-Simons theory
summary: We consider boundary conditions of two-dimensional Dirac fermions which preserve a non-anomalous continuous symmetry which acts differently on the left- and right-movers. Such boundaries are equivalent to topological defects of Weyl fermions preserving the symmetry. We give a general construction of such defects for conformally-embedded symmetries using Chern-Simons theory. They always exist and can be realised as half-space gauging defects for some finite categorical symmetry. Using this technology, we compute the twist lines to which fermions become attached upon scattering through the defect, the boundary central charge of the corresponding folded boundary state, and its mod-2 valued SPT class. As applications, we first consider abelian symmetries and find agreement with known results in the literature. We then study a novel example where an $SU(2) \times SU(4) \times U(1)^2$ symmetry is preserved. In contrast to the abelian case, the twist lines are intrinsically non-invertible and belong to either a $\text{TY}(\mathbb{Z}_3 \times \mathbb{Z}_3)$ or $\text{Rep}(\mathbb{S}_3) \times \mathbb{Z}_3$ symmetry depending on whether scattering is to the left or the right.

title: Flexible Proposal Distributions for Gravitational-Wave Population Inference with Gaussian Mixture Models
summary: Population analyses of gravitational-wave (GW) sources use hierarchical Bayesian inference to constrain astrophysical models while accounting for selection effects. The likelihood is usually estimated by Monte Carlo integration over finite sets of event posterior samples and simulated injections. As catalogs grow, more samples are needed to control the Monte Carlo variance, but the available event samples are fixed by parameter estimation. Sharp population features can also lie in regions poorly sampled by the event posteriors. We fit Gaussian mixture models (GMMs) to the event posteriors and evaluate the likelihood by importance sampling with two proposals: an ensemble of event posteriors and a mixture of that ensemble with a fiducial population. Together with a GMM representation of detected injections, this allows additional samples to be drawn for both event and selection integrals. Increasing the sample count reduces Monte Carlo variance but leaves uncertainty from fitting the densities to finite training sets. In simulated catalogs, the GMM-based estimators show no detectable additional bias relative to the posterior-sample estimator; their calibration is comparable within the limitations of the tests. An application to GWTC-3 with a different mass model gives consistent results across the estimators. The method separates the numerical sampling budget from the original sample count, while requiring explicit checks of density-fit uncertainty and approximation error.

title: Meson-isospectral pair interactions and the residual three-quark force
summary: Meson-isospectral pair rotations can closely reproduce low-lying baryon energies while producing a substantial connected action under their consistent three-body embedding. Starting from an independently calibrated S-wave meson model, we compare ground-mass fits, joint ground-level and gap fits, and direct minimization of the connected remainder. With eighteen shared coefficients, a four-packet joint fit reproduces the nine calibration ground masses and first gaps with RMS errors of $\JointGroundTrain$ and $\JointGapTrain$ MeV, respectively. The excluded ground masses and gaps have RMS errors of $10.7$ and $8.1$ MeV in the same enlarged radial space. Its connected action on the eighteen calibrated inputs is $\JointActionCal$ times the unrotated source action. Eigenvalue agreement and removal of the connected interaction thus impose different tests. Separately optimizing the action with five packets gives a normalized residual of $\ShortActionAll$ for an intermediate-distance fifth packet; a long-distance extension also leaves a substantial remainder. An eliminated-state construction realizes the central color--color structure of an intermediate-configuration mechanism together with correlated pair dressing. These results favor a connected operator basis with three fitted strengths as an economical description within the tested pair family, and quantify its relation to the representation freedom of equivalent few-body Hamiltonians.

title: Impact of Gaia-Sausage-Enceladus merger revealed by a single cosmic clock: thick-to-thin disc transition, gas disc shrinking and bar formation
summary: Whether the formation of the Galactic bar was connected to the Gaia-Sausage-Enceladus (GSE) merger, the last significant merger experienced by the Milky Way, remains an open question. The bar formation epoch has been inferred from the star formation history of the nuclear stellar disc (NSD) traced by Mira variables, and the GSE merger epoch from the age-metallicity relation of red giants. However, these epochs rest on different stellar tracers with different age scales and cannot be compared directly. We recalibrate the Mira period-age relation onto the age scale of APOGEE red giants, with ages from a Bayesian neural network trained on Kepler asteroseismic ages. We fit the Gaia DR3 proper motions of 2394 O-rich disc Mira variables with an action-based quasi-isothermal distribution function whose parameters vary with period, and derive the period-age relation by matching their vertical velocity dispersion as a function of period to that of the APOGEE red giants as a function of age in Funakoshi et al. (2025). This places the NSD star-formation rise and peak at 8.5-10.5 Gyr ago on the red giant age scale, overlapping with the final stage of the GSE-induced starburst, thick-to-thin disc transition and the contraction of the star-forming gas disc. If NSD star formation traces bar formation, these coincidences suggest a possible scenario in which the GSE seeded the bar formation, while fresh gas supplied by the GSE and outer disc gas driven inward by its tidal torques, increased the baryonic dominance of the inner Galaxy.

title: SIGNN++: Robust Graph Neural Star Identification on Earth
summary: We present SIGNN++, a learning-based star identification (SID) framework for celestial navigation in GNSS-denied nighttime environments. Although researchers have developed learning-based SID methods to improve robustness to observation noise, prior evaluations have focused mainly on synthetic or non-terrestrial environments, leaving their reliability under real terrestrial conditions unclear. To address these limitations, SIGNN++ extends SIGNN, a graph neural network-based SID method, with three components: a more realistic noise model for training data, Fourier Transform (FT) of angular-distance edge features, and RANSAC-based Perspective Star Alignment for identification and attitude refinement. The results show that SIGNN++ is more robust to terrestrial observation disturbances and achieves higher star identification accuracy and solved rates than the original SIGNN and publicly available SID baselines, while maintaining comparable attitude accuracy and practical computation time for continuous operation. The implementation code of SIGNN++ and datasets will be available at https://signnpp.github.io/signnpp/.

title: Towards Systematic Control of the Nucleon Gluon PDF with the Pseudo-PDF Method
summary: We present updated lattice quantum chromodynamics (QCD) results for the unpolarized nucleon gluon parton distribution function (PDF) using the pseudo-PDF methodology. The calculation is performed at valence pion masses $M_π\approx 310$ and $690$ MeV on an $a \approx 0.06$ fm ensemble with $2+1+1$ flavors of highly improved staggered quarks (HISQ) generated by the MILC Collaboration. This lattice spacing is finer than those used in previous gluon pseudo-PDF studies, providing access to multiple short-distance separations and nucleon boost momenta as high as $4.4$ GeV. To control excited-state contamination and reduce model dependence, we employ the recently developed Lanczos method, finding good agreement with our previous two-state fit approach. Higher-twist contributions and discretization effects are accounted for through explicit parameterizations in fits to the renormalized short-distance matrix elements. Together, these advances represent important steps toward systematically controlled, high-precision extractions of the gluon PDF. The resulting PDFs exhibit no statistically significant dependence on the valence pion mass and indicate a strongly suppressed gluon distribution at large $x$, consistent with a subset of phenomenological PDF extractions. These results demonstrate progress toward providing systematically controlled lattice-QCD constraints for future global PDF analyses.

title: Density-split analyses of the pairwise kinetic Sunyaev-Zeldovich effect
summary: We consider the dependence of the kinetic Sunyaev-Zeldovich (kSZ) effect on the environments of foreground cosmological structures. Standard pairwise kSZ estimators exploit the fact that galaxies below separations of $\sim 200\,h^{-1}{\rm M}_\odot$ fall towards each other on average, yielding a negative mean pairwise kSZ signal. However, this signal is the residual from a near-cancellation between outflows from underdense regions and infall towards overdensities giving a large variance in the pairwise velocity distribution and hence a low signal-to-noise ratio for the mean kSZ signal. This effect is especially marked at the largest scales, where the pairwise velocity distribution becomes more symmetric about zero. We show that splitting galaxies according to their local overdensity allows the convergence and divergence flows to be separated, yielding pairwise kSZ signals of opposing sign, with a reduction in variance for each subset. We use simulations to perform a detailed analysis of this phenomenon, comparing the cosmological information content in the global pairwise kSZ signal with our new density-split pairwise kSZ estimator. We consider galaxy catalogues comparable to datasets from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument, together with cosmic microwave background instrumental noise characteristic of recent and planned ground-based experiments. We predict that the density-split pairwise kSZ will increase the significance of detection by only a modest factor; nevertheless, we expect improvements by factors of respectively 11 and 4 in constraining $σ_8$ and $Ω_{\rm m}$ when using the combination of Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument and Simons Observatory Large Aperture Telescope surveys.

title: Finding CFTs from spatial positivity of partition functions
summary: We discuss a positivity property for partition functions that generalizes modular invariance and which is here conjectured to hold for general 2D CFTs. We show its relation to positivity properties of Rényi entropies and its meaning in terms of topological defect lines. We apply the conjecture to find consistent local unitary CFT models which are not necessarily modular invariant.

title: Partial geometrization of dark matter in metric $f(R)$ gravity: Exact reconstruction and growth constraints
summary: We ask what fraction of dark matter can be accounted for by the geometry of a stable metric $f(R)$ theory, requiring the expansion history to be exactly equal to that of the $Λ$CDM model. Only a fraction $ξ$ of dark matter clusters as dust, whereas $f(R)$ supplies the rest, as well as $Λ$. We show that the background reconstruction reduces to a linear equation for $F\equiv f_R$, whose solution is $F-1=(1-ξ)\,Θ(a)$, with $Θ$ independent of $ξ$: the departure from general relativity is exactly proportional to the geometrized fraction. We solve this equation in closed form in the matter$+Λ$ and radiation$+$matter eras: in both, the solution is an elementary particular solution plus two hypergeometric modes. Stability requires $F$ to decrease monotonically in time, so $F$ cannot take its general-relativity value $F=1$ both at early and at late times. The effective gravitational coupling $G/F$ therefore necessarily runs: between the radiation era and the de Sitter attractor, $F$ changes by at least $0.837\,(1-ξ)$. In all stable reconstructions but one, $F-1$ grows as $R^{1/3}$ at high curvature, i.e., in dense environments such as the Sun, and local tests of gravity exclude them. The surviving member has $F\to1$ at early times: it recovers general relativity at high curvature and attains the minimal running of $F$. Keeping the linear growth factor at $k=0.1\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ within $10\%$ of its $Λ$CDM value requires $1-ξ\lesssim10^{-3}$, the weakest bound among all stable reconstructions; keeping $σ_8$ within $3\%$ requires $1-ξ\lesssim5\times10^{-5}$. Growth-rate data from DESI DR1 and SDSS DR16 give $1-ξ\lesssim10^{-3}$--$10^{-2}$, and the Cassini bound gives $1-ξ\lesssim10^{-10}$. A smoothly evolving metric $f(R)$ background can therefore geometrize only a negligible fraction of dark matter.

title: Probing imperfect axions with nuclear clocks
summary: We show that $^{229}$Th nuclear clocks can probe departures from the Peccei-Quinn (PQ) solution to the strong CP problem. Explicit PQ breaking or additional CP-violating interactions can shift the minimum of the axion potential and generate CP-violating couplings to matter, inducing a clock response linear in the axion field. We investigate explicit PQ breaking and quark chromo-electric dipole operators as representative realizations of these \textit{imperfect axion} scenarios, consistent with electric dipole moment constraints. For axion dark matter, the linear signal oscillates at the Compton frequency and can dominate the quadratic response. Even without axion dark matter, the Earth can source a static axion field, enabling fifth-force searches with nuclear clocks.

title: The THESAN-ZOOM project: the delayed rise of Lyman continuum escape fractions in bursty high-redshift galaxies
summary: The ionizing radiation that galaxies release into their surroundings depends on whether efficient Lyman continuum (LyC) escape coincides with strong photon production. Stellar feedback can open escape paths as the source population fades, linking the escaping radiation to a galaxy's recent history. We investigate this timing in thirteen high-redshift (z > 3) target haloes from the THESAN-ZOOM radiation-hydrodynamic simulations, post-processed with COLT radiative transfer and sampled at ~10 Myr intervals. The clearest delayed relationship links $\text{SFR}_{10}/\text{SFR}_{100}$ to the LyC escape fraction. Selecting the nearest positive cross-correlation peak gives typical lags of ~16 Myr and peak correlations of 0.4-0.6 in massive haloes, with longer and less coherent delays towards lower masses. The fitted delays scale approximately as $M_\star^{-0.19}$ and $M_\text{halo}^{-0.27}$, although the shortest lags approach the native snapshot spacing. Recurrent variations span multiple amplitude-dependent timescales, consistent with repeated episodes of star formation and feedback. Recent star formation closely tracks both intrinsic and escaping photon rates, while the escape fraction reflects the evolving gas transparency. The H$α$-to-UV luminosity ratio retains a delayed association with escape, offering an observable connection between burst phase and leakage. High transparency during a fading phase can nevertheless yield little escaping radiation. The temporal overlap of photon production and transmission therefore shapes both the amount and timing of escaping radiation, informing the interpretation of observed leakers and their contribution to cosmic reionization.

title: Astro2Method: Benchmarking LLMs on Machine Learning Method Selection in Astronomy
summary: Machine learning (ML) is increasingly used in astronomy, but choosing a suitable method for a scientific problem often requires expertise in both astronomy and ML. Large language models (LLMs) could help astronomers make such choices, yet this ability remains underexplored in existing benchmarks. We introduce Astro2Method, a benchmark of 500 expert-reviewed binary questions from 346 astronomy papers (2024/01-2026/06), based on clear performance differences and complete (Easy) or partial (Hard) explanations from the authors. Across five LLMs, direct prompting achieves 87.50-92.55% accuracy on Easy questions but only 58.87-64.52% on Hard. Using historical papers, neither retrieval-augmented generation nor most agent methods with additional reasoning or retrieval (including ReAct, Self-Ask, and CRITIC) bring consistent improvement. Agents required to search the web improve accuracy mainly when they find the papers the questions are based on, with no consistent improvement otherwise. Providing the source paper's pipeline description with method names masked improves Hard accuracy, matching or exceeding web search. Together, these results suggest that relevant experimental information helps distinguish ML methods, but inferring it from related studies and domain knowledge remains challenging for LLMs in astronomy.

title: Thermomagnetic enhancement of conserved-charge correlations in a lattice-constrained PNJL model
summary: Conserved-charge correlations offer a promising probe of magnetic fields in strongly interacting matter. We investigate their magnetic response and the finite-density equation of state within a lattice-constrained three-flavor Polyakov--Nambu--Jona-Lasinio model. A thermomagnetic scalar coupling, inferred by Gaussian process regression from lattice QCD results for the average light-quark condensate, incorporates inverse magnetic catalysis into the effective interaction. Without fitting conserved-charge observables, the resulting framework substantially improves their magnetic-field dependence and crossover behavior compared with the fixed-coupling model. In particular, it captures the pronounced magnetic enhancement of the baryon--electric-charge correlation and related susceptibility ratios, supporting their use as QCD magnetometers. The comparison demonstrates that the medium dependence of the effective interaction is essential to describe this response within the model. We further calculate pressure Taylor coefficients through sixth order and reconstruct the pressure and baryon density at nonzero baryon chemical potential. Our results show that lattice information from a single chiral observable constrains a broad thermodynamic response, connecting inverse magnetic catalysis, conserved-charge correlations, and the equation of state in a common framework. This provides a lattice-constrained basis for investigating magnetic-field signatures and finite-density thermodynamics in QCD matter.

title: Optimal cosmological cross-correlation analysis with U-Net-based processing
summary: Cosmological cross-correlation analyses are commonly based on two-point statistics, which are optimal for Gaussian random fields but do not capture all relevant information in the presence of non-Gaussianity, which is ubiquitous in late-time cosmic fields. This motivates investigations of higher order statistics, and one method is to use machine learning to construct a correlation-optimized tracer field that can utilize cross-correlation information beyond two-point statistics. Using a tracer field as input and a paired target field as part of the cost function, we test whether a U-Net can learn a transformed tracer field that maximally correlates with the target field. We train a 1D U-Net on paired simulated fields and study controlled cases based on Gaussian and log-normal random fields. We train and quantify performance using the Pearson correlation coefficient with the target field and compare the network output with the analytic linear solution known in the Gaussian limit. For Gaussian fields, the U-Net reproduces the expected linear solution closely and behaves as an effective matched filter in frequency space. For log-normal fields, the network departs from the linear estimator and achieves an improved correlation with the target field, increasing the mean Pearson correlation from 0.857 for the linear estimator to 0.953 for the U-Net output. This indicates that the network is sensitive to information beyond the power spectrum. These controlled 1D experiments show that U-Net-based tracer transformation can effectively extract correlation-relevant information beyond the power spectrum, providing a promising framework for enhancing cosmological cross-correlation analyses.

title: Collinear Gluons from Gravity: Poincaré-Birkhoff-Witt Decomposition and Twisted Intersections
summary: We give an explicit reconstruction of subleading collinear Yang--Mills amplitudes from one-graviton amplitudes in Einstein--Yang--Mills theory and its string corrections. We realize the monodromy kernel in the mixed open-closed string relation as a weighted Lie-algebraic recursion on words of gluon labels. At order $α'^r$, its output contains at most $r$ Lie factors. The Poincaré--Birkhoff--Witt (PBW) theorem decomposes the space spanned by gluon orderings into sectors whose dimensions are given by unsigned Stirling numbers of the first kind. Appropriate shuffle sums of one-graviton amplitudes extract the degree-$r$ sector, for which the string-period matrix drops out. Accordingly, we show that the reconstruction coefficients factor into linear kinematic factors over the product of bipartition factors. Finally, we express the reconstruction coefficients as twisted intersection numbers between Parke--Taylor forms and explicit forest cocycles constructed recursively from logarithmic four-point differentials.

title: Wormhole geometries and energy conditions in linear and non-linear $f(Q,L_m)$ gravity
summary: This study explores static and spherically symmetric wormhole configurations in an extended formulation of symmetric teleparallel gravity governed by $f(Q,L_m)=α(-Q)+βL_m $ and $f(Q,L_m)= -Q+L_m^α $ (where $Q$ is the non-metricity scalar, $L_m$ is the matter Lagrangian, and $α, β$ are constants). By varying the action with respect to the metric, we obtain the corresponding field equations. We conclude that the linear $f(Q,L_m)=α(-Q)+βL_m$ framework successfully supports physically realistic wormholes without requiring extreme energy condition violations. It has been demonstrated that spacetime solutions violating both the radial and lateral null energy conditions in general relativity can nevertheless satisfy the NEC in $f(Q, L_m)$ gravity. Within non-linear $f(Q,L_m)$ gravity, non-exotic asymptotically flat wormhole solutions are derived using linear and asymptotically linear equations of state. Our results open new avenues to link modified gravity models with the observable astrophysical traits of exotic spacetimes.

title: Faithful Uncertainties in ML-Based Inverse Problems: GPs, NNs and NTKs for the Triplet PDF
summary: Machine-learning methods are increasingly used to solve inverse problems in physics, where a faithful estimate of the uncertainty on the reconstructed function is as important as its central value. We address this question in the simplest instance of a parton distribution function (PDF) determination: the reconstruction of the non-singlet triplet distribution $T_3(x,Q_0^2)$ from deep-inelastic scattering data. Within a closure-test framework, in which the underlying PDF is known and the pseudo-data carry correlated experimental uncertainties, we compare Gaussian processes with different kernels, neural-network ensembles trained with different loss functions, and empirical neural tangent kernel approximations. We find that methods yielding comparable central reconstructions can produce markedly different uncertainties, and we identify the ingredients that control them: a likelihood that includes the full experimental covariance, the functional prior encoded in the kernel or in the endpoint preprocessing, and, for tangent-kernel approximations, the stage of training at which the kernel is evaluated. A normalised-bias diagnostic shows that calibration depends on the correlations of the predictive covariance, not only on its pointwise width. Our results illustrate why closure tests and covariance-aware diagnostics are essential to validate uncertainties in ML-based approaches to inverse problems.

title: The black hole-galaxy correlations of the 12 micron local AGN sample: a NuSTAR perspective
comment: 12 pages, 9 figures (+ Appendix), accepted for publication in Astronomy and Astrophysics
summary: The M-sigma correlation of inactive galaxies plays a crucial role in estimating the black hole mass (MBH) in active galactic nuclei (AGN): 1) it is used to calibrate the reverberation mapping (RM) method; 2) the RM is the basis of the single epoch method, the most-used technique to determine MBH of broad-line AGN; and 3) in narrow-line AGN, MBH is often directly inferred from the M-sigma correlation. The main goal of this work is to test whether the M-sigma relation calibrated from inactive galaxies can be reliably applied to a local AGN population spanning Seyfert 1, Seyfert 2, and hidden broad-line region galaxies (HBLRs), and whether the resulting AGN relation has sufficient predictive power to be used as an indirect MBH estimator. To investigate this hypothesis, we used the 12 micron AGN sample, a local representative and largely unbiased sample. Since a substantial fraction of this sample has good-quality NuSTAR data, we estimated their MBH with the X-ray scaling method, which works for any AGN accreting at moderate or high level. We find that the M-sigma correlation of the 12 micron AGN sample is different from the one obtained with inactive galaxies and has a substantial scatter. Therefore, its predictive power for MBH estimates is fairly limited. We also find that the MBH-Mgal correlation based on the 12 micron AGN sample is consistent with the analogous correlation obtained from a large sample of nearby type 1 AGN and inconsistent with that of inactive galaxies. Finally, we find suggestive evidence that Seyfert 1 and HBLRs have similar and systematically higher Eddington ratios than Seyfert 2 galaxies.

title: A Technical Reanalysis of the Viking Carbon Assimilation-Pyrolytic Release Experiment
comment: 23 pages, 2 figures, 1 table. Submitted to Astrobiology
summary: The 1976 Viking Carbon Assimilation-Pyrolytic Release (CAPyR) experiment tested whether carbon from $^{14}$CO$_2$ and $^{14}$CO entered Martian soil during a 120-hour incubation in a form retained during a 120 $^\circ$C purge but released by pyrolysis at 635 $^\circ$C. Untrapped radioactivity was measured as Peak 1; material retained in an organic vapor trap was oxidized and measured as Peak 2. Net Peak 2 was intended to represent synthesized reduced organic carbon. Seven of nine usable incubations at Chryse and Utopia Planitia yielded significant net Peak 2 signals, including the dark U1 run. An underreported Viking Lander 2 gas leak introduces uncertainty into U1-U3. The C1 signal corresponds to approximately 10 or 30 pmol of carbon, assuming derivation entirely from CO or CO$_2$, respectively. We reassess these results in light of the possible presence of perchlorate salts in Viking soils. Oxidation of fixed organic radiocarbon during pyrolysis could have shifted label from Peak 2 to Peak 1, a perchlorate-specific effect not considered in previous CAPyR analyses. Hubbard's (1979) mineral-substrate experiments produced abiotic Peak 2 signals without reproducing the heat sensitivity. No demonstrated abiotic mechanism has reproduced all CAPyR observations under Mars-relevant conditions. The observations remain consistent with a biological carbon-assimilation system whose relevant activity survives C5's 120 $^\circ$C/90 $^\circ$C pretreatment but is strongly impaired by C2's 175 $^\circ$C pretreatment. Together with the Labeled Release experiment, CAPyR suggests oxidative and reductive chemistry in separate aliquots from common Martian soil acquisitions. Metabolically active life combines these processes; a quantitative abiotic explanation of their combined heat-labile response patterns remains to be demonstrated.

title: $N \to Δ$ Transition Form Factors in the Thermal AdS/QCD Soft-Wall Model with Modified Propagators
summary: We investigate electromagnetic (EM) and axial vector (AV) form factors of the nucleon-Delta baryon transition within the thermal AdS/QCD soft-wall model. While the vector bulk-to-boundary propagator admits a well-behaved analytical solution, the transverse axial vector equation of motion involves the vacuum expectation value of the bifundamental scalar (generating chiral symmetry breaking). Due to this, the axial propagator diverges asymptotically, rendering it unsuitable for computing observables in the soft-wall model. To address this problem, we implement a regularization for the axial propagator in the form of a momentum-dependent cut-off, that identifies its correct physical regime. This is achieved via an interior constraint approach to the boundary-value problem, that determines the cut-off point. The consistency of this procedure is verified near the UV limit. As a proof of concept, we test this modified propagator (and also a parametrically deformed version of it) to estimate axial vector form factors of the $N \to Δ$ transition, and find results moderately comparable with form factor profiles from experimental observations, lattice QCD, and other theoretical models. Equipped with this regularization, the thermal soft-wall model becomes a useful tool to probe thermal characteristics of QCD form factors. We demonstrate this for both, the EM and AV sectors of the $N \to Δ$ transition.

title: ULTRAMAN: A Proposed ultrasound detector for macroscopic dark matter
comment: 9 pages with 3 figures, comments very welcome
summary: We propose ULTRAMAN (ULTRAsound Macro ANalyzer), a passive ultrasound array experiment designed to search for macroscopic dark matter (macros) through coherent acoustic disturbances generated as compact objects traverse a controlled target medium. Unlike existing dark matter detectors that primarily rely on scintillation, ionization, or other signatures of energy deposition, ULTRAMAN exploits the acoustic response of matter to reconstruct individual highly supersonic trajectories using synchronized multielement ultrasound arrays. The framework connects macro stopping power and interaction cross section to the resulting acoustic pressure, while the expected event rate probes the macro mass and abundance. A genuine candidate would appear not as an isolated radio frequency spike, but as a correlated multichannel track consistent with a single highly supersonic passage through the target. Representative macro, nuclearite, axion quark nugget, and primordial black hole benchmarks are shown to occupy distinct regions of the resulting acoustic observable space. Existing ultrasound technology offers a realistic route to an event-level terrestrial search for macroscopic dark matter, with null observations translating into complementary constraints on its parameter space.

title: Reentrant $d=2+1$ Superfluidity at High Temperature
summary: We present a UV-complete model with a global $U(1)$ symmetry in $d=2+1$ dimensions that exhibits a Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) ordered phase at arbitrarily high temperatures. A careful separation of scales yields a two-dimensional Euclidean effective field theory whose construction remains perturbatively controlled even when its soft modes become strongly coupled. We determine the BKT phase boundary by carefully matching this theory to existing lattice Monte Carlo results. The high-temperature phase supports gapless static modes and algebraically decaying correlations even as $T\to\infty$.

title: Ricci-flat Seeds, Trombone Rescaling and Magnetizing Kerr Black Holes
summary: We present a new family of Ricci-flat rotating metrics, which we refer to as Solution II, obtained by demagnetizing the genuine Kerr-Bertotti-Robinson (G-KBR) black hole. Together with Solution I, which was previously obtained by demagnetizing the Kerr-Bertotti-Robinson (KBR) black hole, this gives two families of Ricci-flat deformations of the Kerr black hole, each labeled by $B$. We study the global structures, thermodynamics, various limits, and the local connections among these limits. We also study the remagnetizations in both Einstein-Maxwell and Kaluza-Klein theories, and find that, to yield a physically acceptable solution, the Ernst transformation should be augmented by an appropriate trombone rescaling.

title: Probing Heavy Neutral Leptons through New Gauge Interactions at the Forward Physics Facilities
summary: We investigate the prospects for improving the heavy neutral lepton (HNL) searches at the far-forward LHC experiments FASER and FASER$ν$, as well as their proposed HL-LHC successors, FASER2 and FASER$ν$2, using new HNL production mechanisms. We consider scenarios in which HNLs couple directly to a new $U(1)$ gauge boson and decay into visible Standard Model final states through mixing with active neutrinos. Focusing on the $U(1)_{B-L}$, $U(1)_{B-3L_τ}$, and $U(1)_B$ gauge extensions as benchmark models, we study HNL production through proton bremsstrahlung and Drell--Yan processes, which probe complementary mediator-mass regimes. We analyze several visible decay channels, including charged leptons, neutral mesons, and other hadrons, and evaluate the projected sensitivities for different neutrino-flavor mixing patterns. We find that these new production mechanisms that differ qualitatively from the conventional picture in which both production and decay are controlled by active-sterile mixing enable the far-forward LHC program to probe previously unexplored regions of HNL parameter space, with the first-ever demonstration of FASER$ν$ having sensitivity to HNLs and FASER2 and FASER$ν$2 offering substantially enhanced sensitivity during the HL-LHC era, even reaching the canonical seesaw prediction for all three lepton flavors. Our results demonstrate that new gauge interactions can substantially enhance HNL production independently of the active-sterile mixing that governs their visible decays, opening complementary opportunities to explore HNLs at the forward physics facilities.

title: The LBT Y$_{\rm p}$ Project VI: Gas-Phase Chemical Abundance Patterns of Metal-Poor Nebulae
comment: 33 pages, 15 figures, 2 tables, submitted to The Astrophysical Journal. Comments welcome
summary: Through a combined rest-optical and NIR observing campaign, the Large Binocular Telescope Primordial He Abundance ($Y_{\rm p}$) Project has delivered a precision measurement of $Y_{\rm p}$. Given the stringent requirements to measure gas-phase He abundances, the optical spectra contain emission features from a plethora of metals in the Interstellar Medium (ISM). We present gas-phase N, O, Ne, S, Cl, Ar, K and Fe abundance patterns in 62 low-metallicity nebulae. We assess ionization correction factors for each element and select those that reproduce the observed ionic abundance trends. The Ne/O, S/O, and Ar/O abundances do not evolve with metallicity and agree with the solar ratios. Given the Type Ia enrichment of S and Ar, the solar S/O and Ar/O suggest extended star formation histories in local galaxies relative to high-$z$ galaxies at fixed O/H. We report the first ISM K abundances in low-metallicity extragalactic nebulae; both Cl/O and K/O are constant with O/H, indicating the production of these odd-Z elements follows that of $α$ elements. Consistent with prior analyses, gas-phase Fe/O is observed to decrease with O/H due to dust depletion; correcting for this produces an average [Fe/O]$=$$-$0.80, implying Fe-deficient stars capable of producing hard ionizing spectra. Finally, the metallicity-insensitive log(N/O) plateau from 50 nebulae is $-$1.43$\pm$0.10, consistent with previous works. Five galaxies have N/O significantly enhanced relative to the primary plateau, and we discuss their properties, mechanisms that could bias measurements of N/O, and nucleosynthetic progenitors that can produce enhanced N at low metallicity.

title: The Pandora SmallSat: post-launch operations and mission update
comment: 9 pages, 4 figures; paper published as proceedings of the SPIE
summary: The Pandora SmallSat is a NASA flight project designed to study the atmospheres of exoplanets. Transmission spectroscopy of transiting exoplanets provides our best opportunity to identify the makeup of planetary atmospheres in the coming decade, and is a key science driver for HST and JWST. Stellar photospheric inhomogeneity due to star spots, however, has been shown to contaminate the observed spectra in these high-precision measurements. Pandora will address the problem of stellar contamination by collecting long-duration photometric observations sampled over a stellar rotation period with a visible-light channel and simultaneous spectra with a near-IR channel. These simultaneous multiwavelength observations will constrain star spot covering fractions of exoplanet host stars, enabling star and planet signals to be disentangled in transmission spectra to then reliably determine exoplanet atmosphere compositions. Pandora will observe exoplanets with sizes ranging from Earth-size to Jupiter-size and host stars spanning mid-K to late-M spectral types. Pandora was selected in early 2021 as part of NASA's inaugural Astrophysics Pioneers Program. Herein, we present an overview of the mission, including the science objectives, operations, the observatory, science planning, and upcoming milestones as we prepare for launch readiness in 2025.

title: Onsager Algebras and Lattice Fermions
summary: We study the exact Onsager algebra of free lattice fermions in staggered, Wilson, and overlap incarnations, working in both Hamiltonian and Euclidean formulations in four spacetime dimensions. In each case, we show that the exact lattice algebra emanates the full chiral symmetry of the low-energy theory: if there are $N$ massless Dirac fermions in the continuum, the Onsager algebra reduces to a $U(2N)$ chiral symmetry. The details of which generators are quantised or ultra-local differ between formulations. There is also a trade-off between the locality of generators and the maximum compact subgroup of the Onsager algebra.

title: Same Events, Weaker Bound: Model Dependence in Magellanic Microlensing Limits on Primordial Black Holes
summary: OGLE microlensing of the Magellanic Clouds sets the leading bounds on primordial black holes (PBHs) as dark matter from $10^{-8}$ to $10^{3}\,M_\odot$. Holding the detected events and survey efficiencies fixed, we show that changes to the Milky Way halo, the stellar lens populations and the Large Magellanic Cloud halo, each motivated by recent data, weaken the published strict 20-year bound by up to $\simeq6$, and by over an order of magnitude in an extreme stress test. With primordial clustering, the planetary-mass bound weakens by a factor $3.4$--$6$. We strongly recommend that compact-object dark matter limits be quoted together with their modeling assumptions and, generally, be derived under conservative assumptions.

title: Defect flows from functional relations in the asymptotic semiring
comment: 81 pages, 34 figures, 1 Mathematica notebook in the ancillary files
summary: We study perturbations of topological defects by a relevant holomorphic defect field in two-dimensional conformal field theory. This produces translation invariant defects and these necessarily flow to topological defects in the infrared. Translation invariant defects form a monoidal category which extends the fusion category of topological defects. We argue that the renormalisation group flow defines a semiring homomorphism from the semiring of translation invariant defects to an "asymptotic semiring" which we construct from topological defects. The semiring homomorphism preserves functional relations, and we illustrate in the example of Virasoro minimal models that the resulting relations in the asymptotic semiring constrain the defect flow endpoints. The companion paper [1] contains a detailed study of such defect flows in several minimal models, both numerically and analytically.

title: Calculating gravitational waves at infinity: the missing link
summary: Gravitational-wave science requires waveform templates to be computed at future null infinity, the asymptotic boundary of spacetime. Numerical solutions of Einstein's equations typically rely on a Cauchy evolution on a finite computational domain, but can produce waveforms at infinity by performing a subsequent characteristic evolution that compactifies the spacetime. Such waveforms capture expected physical effects, like gravitational-wave memory and late-time, power-law tails. But this characteristic evolution requires initial data consistent with the interior Cauchy solution to avoid producing spurious, long-lived transients. A careful analysis shows that previous prescriptions for this initial data were not sufficiently consistent and provides a way to remedy the problem. The new initial data yield accurate waveforms from the first cycle onward. The construction is independent of the Cauchy formulation and enables the production of catalogs of robust waveforms at infinity.

title: Sequential SBI for Resonance Searches at the LHC
summary: Neural simulation-based inference has been shown to extract significantly more information from LHC data than histogram-based analyses. So far, it has mostly been applied to couplings, for which the polynomial structure of the scattering amplitude can be exploited. Masses and widths instead move and deform the signal in phase space, and learning their likelihood requires many event samples covering the continuous theory parameter space. We show how sequential simulation-based inference can address this by iteratively concentrating the simulations where the observed data points. Using a parton-level example with an exact reference likelihood and reconstruction-level analyses of $A\to ZH\to \ell\ell b\bar b$ and $Y\to HH\to (t\bar t)(t\bar t)$, we demonstrate that sequential training produces significantly more accurate and better calibrated likelihoods than single round training with the same amount of training events.

title: The PAU Survey: Active galactic nucleus galaxies in galaxy pairs
summary: Aims. Leveraging the high-precision photometric redshifts of the Physics of the Accelerating Universe Survey (PAUS), we aim to investigate the connection between active galactic nuclei (AGNs) and galaxy pairs up to redshifts of $\sim1.0$. Methods. We identified 16,824 galaxy pairs with projected separations of $r_p < 100$ kpc and radial-velocity differences of $ΔV < 3500$ km s$^{-1}$. AGNs were selected by cross-matching PAUS galaxies with multi-wavelength AGN catalogues, yielding 270 AGNs in pairs out of a parent sample of 8,880 AGNs in PAUS. We constructed control samples of isolated AGNs; non-AGNs in pairs; and isolated non-AGNs matched in redshift, absolute magnitude, and environment. Results. Active galactic nuclei in pairs show progressively redder rest-frame colours with increasing redshift, particularly at redshifts of $z\gtrsim 0.5$, whereas isolated AGNs and non-AGNs in pairs show no significant colour evolution and remain at $\mathrm{M_g-M_r}\sim0.65$. Pairs hosting AGNs are also preferentially morphologically disturbed interacting systems found at smaller projected separations and velocity offsets, consistent with more dynamically advanced interactions. Conclusions. These results provide evidence of a redshift-dependent link between galaxy interactions and AGN activity, suggesting that interactions play an increasingly important role in triggering nuclear activity at intermediate redshifts. This study highlights the unique capability of PAUS to probe AGN-galaxy interaction connections beyond the local Universe with unprecedented statistical power.

title: Photometric classification and out-of-taxonomy detection of ZTF transients with FLARE
summary: Photometric classifiers decide which of the million nightly alerts of time-domain surveys receive one of the few thousand spectra taken each year, and they are the first place where a transient outside the trained classes can be noticed. We present flare, the photometric classification and anomaly-detection module of AppleCiDEr, evaluated on 10 497 spectroscopically confirmed ZTF transients in six classes and 53 objects from families outside the taxonomy. Catalogue context raises the macro F1 score, with the largest gains where the defining information is absent from the light curve. Blind detection recovers few out-of-taxonomy objects at a 1% false-alarm rate, while a simulated review loop recovers 83% of them after inspecting 15% of the stream. The first confirmations of a new family are most useful in the feature space: with the same eleven labels, a head on the frozen features detects 68% of the tidal disruption events hidden from the training against 57% for a combiner over the anomaly scores, and retraining with them as a new class reaches 85%. The module runs in production on Fritz, the ZTF instance of SkyPortal, and its alarm is reported as a false-alarm rate per unit time on the stream, calibrated on the photometry that the service receives

title: Constraints on interacting dark energy with a constant equation of state in light of DESI DR2: The role of the interaction term
summary: Recent DESI baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) analyses suggest a preference for an evolving dark energy equation of state (EoS) that crosses the phantom divide $w=-1$. Interactions between dark energy and dark matter can also produce an apparent phantom-divide crossing in the effective dark energy EoS. In this work, we investigate interacting dark energy (IDE) models with a constant EoS parameter $w$, using cosmic microwave background (CMB) observations from Planck, ACT, and SPT, DESI DR2 BAO measurements, and type Ia supernova data from PantheonPlus, DES-Dovekie, and DESY5. We consider four typical forms of the interaction term $Q$. Our results show that the IDE models with $Q\proptoρ_{\rm de}$ generally exhibit a stronger preference for nonzero dark-sector interactions. In particular, for the CMB+DESI+DES-Dovekie data, the IDE model with $Q=βH_0ρ_{\rm de}$ yields $β=-2.52^{+0.80}_{-0.54}$ and $w=-1.510^{+0.170}_{-0.120}$, corresponding to deviations from $β=0$ and $w=-1$ at the $3.2σ$ and $3.0σ$ levels, respectively. Interestingly, the effective EoS of the IDE model with $Q=βH_0ρ_{\rm de}$ exhibits a redshift evolution resembling that of the $w_0w_a$CDM model, crossing the phantom divide. Bayesian evidence further indicates that this IDE model is favored over $Λ$CDM and the other three IDE models. Our analysis helps identify which interaction forms better account for current cosmological observations.

title: From bulk flows to boundary generators and costs
summary: Holographic complexity admits a broad family of bulk observables, yet their relation to boundary state-preparation costs remains unclear. We propose a local prescription that associates suitable bulk observables with quadratic cost geometries on families of states prepared by Euclidean sources. Building on the holographic transport of bulk Hamiltonian flows to Euclidean preparation sources, we use the Hessian of the transported generator at a stationary reference state to define a candidate cost metric. When this Hessian is positive definite, the minimised preparation energy reproduces the change in the bulk observable to quadratic order. We characterise the resulting preparation penalties relative to the Fubini-Study metric and compute them for the maximal volume in scalar perturbations of AdS$_3$. At large-conformal dimension, we recover the known proportionality between cost and Fubini-Study metrics. At finite dimension, we obtain positive but generally unequal penalties for source variations that displace the bulk field and its conjugate momentum, breaking this proportionality even for a single scalar operator. We further study a deformation of volume by quadratic scalar and gradient terms in the large-dimension regime, determining how the couplings modify the penalties and constrain positivity. These additions selectively change field-displacement costs, with the gradient term introducing mode dependence. Our results provide an explicit local connection between the choice of bulk observables and the assignment of boundary preparation penalties.

title: Accurate initial data for Cauchy-characteristic evolution
summary: Accurate gravitational-wave (GW) templates from numerical-relativity (NR) simulations are essential for GW science. These templates are typically computed at finite radii and extrapolated to future null infinity $\mathscr{I}^{+}$, the asymptotic boundary of spacetime. However, this procedure is known to not accurately capture momentum fluxes and memory effects, limiting the accuracy of waveform models and data analyses that rely on them. Cauchy-characteristic evolution (CCE) instead integrates Einstein's equations along outgoing null hypersurfaces from a Cauchy simulation's finite-radius worldtube to $\mathscr{I}^{+}$. Its accuracy, though, has been limited by initial data that produce long-lived spurious transients, which contaminate several cycles of the waveform emitted by the binary coalescence. We identify incorrect initial angular coordinates as the source of these transients. We construct initial data that matches the Cauchy worldtube data through second order in the radial derivatives and solve for the angular coordinates consistent with the resulting radial profile. These improvements remove the unphysical transient: a $10\%$ modulation of a binary black hole's $(2,2)$ mode amplitude lasting over $1000\,M$ disappears, and the late-time tail of a head-on black hole collision is recovered. The construction is independent of the Cauchy formulation and allows archived simulations to be reprocessed with CCE, paving the way for improved GW catalogs.

title: Continuous Measurement of Quantum Axion Dark Matter
summary: We provide a fully quantum-mechanical description of the continuous measurement of wavelike dark matter. Our focus is cavity haloscopes, although our results inform a broad range of axion searches. We extend the input-output formalism by treating the axion as a quantum field, finding how its quantum state is imprinted onto higher-order moments of observables of the outgoing transmission-line modes. We further develop a novel measurement-record formalism, which computes the joint probability distribution of all measurement outcomes and is well suited to studying the axion in the time domain. With it, we compute the exact axion-induced number distribution for the first time, demonstrating that it is not Poisson. We argue that virialized axion dark matter is expected to be in a Gaussian quantum state, and show that number or quadrature measurements can distinguish this from the predictions of a coherent state or even a Bose-Einstein condensate. Finally, we show that intrinsically quantum effects, such as those from Fock or squeezed axion states, are far too weak to detect.

title: Optical-Infrared Extinction Variation in Nearby Molecular Clouds
summary: The dust extinction curve is an important probe of the properties of dust grains, particularly their size distribution. The properties of dust grains are expected to change significantly in dense molecular clouds due to shielding from interstellar radiation and increased frequency of grain-grain and grain-gas collisions. We measure the dust extinction curve shape parameter R(V) in 9 nearby, dense molecular clouds using data from the APOGEE spectroscopic survey, in combination with ten-band photometry from PS1, 2MASS, and WISE. We analyze the results to determine how the extinction curve varies in nearby molecular clouds. We find that most molecular clouds show a positive correlation between R(V) and E(B-V), but the strength of the correlation varies significantly between clouds. In addition, we find that the clouds with the strongest correlation tend to have very high dispersion in R(V) at fixed E(B-V), which tightens dramatically when clouds are subdivided into separate regions. This suggests that local environmental conditions beyond density shape the R(V)-E(B-V) relation.

title: Astrometric detection of rocky exoplanets from inexpensive space platforms
comment: In Proc. SPIE 14145, Space Telescopes and Instrumentation 2026: Optical, Infrared, and Millimeter Wave, 1414510 (21 Aug 2026)
summary: The detection of orbiting exoplanets by way of astrometric monitoring of the host star to reveal gravitationally induced reflex motion requires extreme precision and measurement stability when targeting Earth-mass objects. Despite this, astrometry is widely regarded as the most promising avenue for the most desired of all targets: true Earth analogue systems in the solar neighbourhood. Formerly thought to require flagship class investment, recently several smaller concepts such as the TOLIMAN and SHERA missions have shown that detections are possible, at least in principle, from more modest space platforms. A key enabling feature is that these missions exploit narrow-angle astrometry. Observing only multiple star systems where the target provides its own astrometric reference greatly alleviates the challenges confronted by traditional astrometry with its reliance on distant, faint field stars. This principle underlies the TOLIMAN mission, for which progress and status is reported. However, only a tiny handful of nearby star systems are suited to such a TOLIMAN-like architecture. This paper discusses speculative optical concepts featuring ultra-stable telescopes of modest (<0.5m) aperture designed for astrometric monitoring of isolated single stars at the micro-arcsecond scales required for the discovery of Earth mass objects orbiting sun-like stars in temperate orbits. In simulation, highly sought-after neighbourhood systems such as Epsilon Eridani and Tau Ceti can be exhaustively searched for rocky planets with dedicated observing campaigns spanning several years, all from relatively inexpensive orbital platforms.

title: GPAge: a Global Parameterization based on cosmic Age for some unified early-time and late-time solutions to the Hubble tension
summary: The over $5σ$ Hubble tension continues to motivate modifications of the standard $Λ$-cold-dark-matter ($Λ\rm CDM$) model. The large number of proposed resolutions for the Hubble tension, broadly divided into early- and late-time solutions, motivates phenomenological parametrizations to constrain the viable solution space. Recently, there is a growing interest in unifying early- and late-time solutions. In this work, we extend the original Parametrization based on cosmic Age (PAge) to cover both the early and late Universe. Specifically, we incorporate the radiation-dominated epoch at the background level and complete the perturbation sector within a unified-dark-fluid framework. The resulting parametrization can accurately reproduce target cosmological models at both the background and perturbation levels. Confronting this global PAge with cosmological observations, we find that it improves the best fit relative to $Λ\rm CDM$, but does not raise $H_0$ significantly enough to alleviate the Hubble tension. Our parametrizations indicate that varying the early-time matter-like density, even together with a flexible late-time expansion history, is insufficient to resolve the Hubble tension. These results suggest that resolving the Hubble tension requires pre-recombination physics beyond a simple retuning of the matter-like density.

title: 3D de Sitter from complex Virasoro TQFT: Observers and knots
summary: The Euclidean saddles of 3D Einstein gravity with positive cosmological constant are spherical three-manifolds. When one adds a heavy observer, the backreacted saddles are spherical cone manifolds, with a conical singularity along the observer worldline. We propose exact gravitational partition functions at fixed topology on a class of spherical cone manifolds that undergo hyperbolic-to-spherical transitions as the cone angles increase. Our construction relies on a careful analytic continuation of the product of two Virasoro TQFT partition functions. We test the proposal by showing that the exact partition functions exponentiate in the semiclassical limit to the spherical volume, in agreement with the gravitational on-shell action. This leads to a spherical volume conjecture for the product of continued Virasoro TQFT amplitudes. As further evidence, we relate the theta and tetrahedron graph amplitudes to the two-point function and out-of-time-ordered four-point function of operators on a massive observer's worldline. In appropriate limits, we recover the static patch scalar two-point function with finite observer backreaction and the semiclassical effects of observer recoil. In addition, we analyze examples with knotted worldlines and reproduce their spherical volumes. We also apply our prescription to Seifert manifolds, which are off-shell in AdS$_3$ gravity but admit dS$_3$ saddles, and find agreement with their spherical volumes semiclassically. Finally, using Dehn surgery on torus knots and links, we obtain partition functions on smooth spherical three-manifolds.

title: Quintaverse-Phantiverse Cosmologies in $f(Q,C)$ Gravity: a Non-coincident Geometrical Origin of Cosmic Acceleration
summary: We investigate the asymptotic dark energy sectors of a quadratic form of $f(Q,C)$ Lagrangian. We reformulate the original equations of motion to obtain the equivalent dynamical system, for two non-trivial classes of affine connections allowed by symmetries of $f(Q,C)$ gravity. In these scenarios, the late-time accelerated expansion emerges as an intrinsic geometrical effect of the $f(Q,C)$ sector, without invoking an independent dark energy component. We find that an effective dark matter solution emerges for one class, whereas for the other class, the positivity of the matter density and the conservation of the momentum tensor cannot be simultaneously satisfied. This leads to the conclusion that there exists an effective dark matter solution for which the matter contribution is a combination of a pressureless matter as well as a stiff fluid. Furthermore, in both cases there always exists a universal stable accelerated expansion solution. Besides, the matter solutions are saddle points for those values of the model parameters that ensure the conservation of the energy momentum. In addition, we introduce a parameterization in which the equation of state parameter at the fixed point corresponding to accelerated expansion is characterized by a free parameter that quantifies its deviation from $-1$. We thereby inspired to invent the terms ``Quintaverse'' and ``Phantiverse'', corresponding to quintessence-like and phantom-like attractor solutions. Also, we numerically illustrate the evolution of different cosmological quantities and the phase-space diagrams. Particularly, the behavior of the Universe using two kinematic toolkits, namely, the cosmographic and statefinder variables, is discussed.

title: Neutrino Transition Polarizability
summary: We study Neutrino Transition Polarizability, where a light pseudoscalar $φ$ couples active neutrinos to heavy neutral leptons $N$ and interacts with two photons. We consider an effective description of the active - sterile interaction, and a realization within the inverse seesaw mechanism; the coupling to photons is generated by heavy charged states. For $m_N>m_φ$, the decay $N\toνφ$ can greatly shorten the heavy neutrino lifetime, while $φ\toγγ$ produces a displaced photon pair. This changes the relevant search strategies, favoring production and decay inside detectors. We discuss existing constraints and estimate the sensitivity of displaced photon searches at DUNE, Belle II, LHCb and FCC-ee, highlighting the complementarity of neutrino scattering and meson and electroweak boson decays.

title: Optical and near-infrared s-process abundance scales in the Galactic disc
comment: 10 pages, 5 figures. Accepted for publication in A&A
summary: A discrepancy has recently emerged between optical and near-infrared (NIR) s-process abundance scales, particularly for Neodymium (Nd). We investigated this issue using a direct cross-match between the optical Gaia-ESO Survey (DR5) and NIR SDSS-V/MWM (DR19). While atmospheric parameters and Cerium (Ce) abundances exhibit robust 1:1 correlations, Nd displays a systematic X-shaped vertical stretching. Our analysis reveals that the SDSS-V pipeline expands intrinsic Nd variations by a scaling factor of 5.54 relative to the stable optical baseline. This phenomenon is driven by baseline compression in the APOGEE H-band, where the growth of the molecular forest (CN and CO) at high metallicities depresses the local continuum. This forces the chi^2 minimisation engine in the NIR abundance determination to inflate derived abundances to reach mathematical convergence. We provide an empirical calibration framework to reconcile these disparate regimes. This correction effectively eliminates the contradictory negative radial [Nd/Fe] gradient of -0.052 dex/kpc reported in recent NIR surveys, bringing them into alignment with the rising trends established by the optical high-resolution Gaia-ESO survey. These results demonstrate that the observed scale expansion is a spectroscopic artefact of line-blanketing rather than a physical Galactic trend.

title: Science-driven design and performance evaluation of a Silicon Laue Component lens for hard X-ray polarimetry
comment: 6 pages. 2 figures. Submitted to Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary:
Focusing hard X-rays above 80 keV is challenging for grazing-incidence optics. Laue lenses offer an alternative based on crystal diffraction. We assess a lens based on Silicon Laue Components (SiLCs), consisting of stacked silicon plates, for polarimetry of accreting stellar-mass black holes and strongly magnetized neutron stars in the 80-200 keV band.
  We derive effective-area requirements from the minimum detectable polarization at 99% confidence (MDP99) for an XL-Calibur-inspired polarimeter observing a 100-mCrab source for 100 ks. We evaluate an 18-m-focal-length lens combining Si(220) and Si(111) reflections, with a 63 arcsec diffraction bandpass and a 90% optical filling factor, using on-axis ray tracing of a perfectly aligned lens with uniform crystal curvatures.
  An MDP99 of 5% requires mean effective areas of approximately 260, 400, and 740 cm^2 in the 80-100, 100-130, and 130-200 keV bands, respectively. The lens spans radii of 356-1453 mm and continuously covers 80-200 keV. Its effective area reaches approximately 375 cm^2 near the low-energy boundary and falls to approximately 200 cm^2 at 180 keV. The focal-plane diameters enclosing 50% and 90% of the focused signal are 5.4 mm (62 arcsec) and 9.8 mm (112 arcsec). Mean effective areas of approximately 320, 250, and 220 cm^2 give reference MDP99 values of approximately 4.5%, 6.4%, and 9.5% in the three bands.
  The design reaches few-percent polarimetric sensitivity below 100 keV but does not maintain a 5% MDP99 across 80-200 keV under the adopted detector assumptions. It remains relevant for more strongly polarized hard components and provides a reference for end-to-end optimization of the optics, detector response, and background.

title: Assessing the consistency of the CPL dark-energy model with cosmological data: Simulation-calibrated neural posterior disagreement
summary: Recent DESI observations hint at a preference for dynamical dark energy with an equation of state that crosses the phantom divide within the Chevallier-Polarski-Linder (CPL) parameterization. In this work, we assess the consistency of the CPL parameterization with current cosmological observations. We develop a model check based on the disagreement between posteriors inferred by neural posterior estimation and flow-matching posterior estimation. Both estimators are trained on the same CPL simulations, and their posterior disagreement is calibrated using independent simulations to obtain a global $p$-value. Controlled simulations assess the reliability of the calibrated \(p\)-values and show how detection sensitivity depends on the form of departure from the assumed model. Applying the test to the compressed CMB+DESI+DESY5 data vector yields $p_{\rm global}=0.524$, indicating that the current observations are consistent with the CPL model. The method has a median evaluation time of only $0.53\,{\rm s}$, enabling efficient assessments of cosmological model adequacy. This framework enables efficient tests of dark-energy models, providing a firmer basis for investigating the physical origin of cosmic acceleration.

title: Big Crunching Your Big Bang: Doubly Warped Time-Dependent Type II Flux Backgrounds and Scale Separation
summary: We construct three analytic, doubly warped cosmological solutions of massless type IIA supergravity with different choices of fluxes, namely, $H_3$, $\tilde F_2$ and $\tilde F_4$ along internal directions. The $H_3$ solution also belongs to the common NS--NS sector of type IIB. Our solutions show that, without localised sources, nonconstant warping on a smooth compact space is possible. We derive their eleven-dimensional uplifts and four-dimensional Einstein-frame cosmology. Each universe undergoes (decelerating) expansion from a Big Bang, reaches a maximum size, and undergoes contraction towards a Big Crunch. We also analyse the scale separation of these backgrounds and find that they exhibit a small Einstein frame Hubble scale to KK mass ratio $\frac{|H_E|}{m_{\mathrm{KK}}}\ll1,$ although for a brief period of time, around the maxima of the scale factor in the Einstein frame. Finally, we analyse the supersymmetry of these backgrounds, which demonstrates that all three solutions break all forms of type IIA supersymmetry.

title: Black Hole Shadows and Quasinormal Modes with Dark Matter at the Horizon
summary: In this work, we study the effect of a surrounding dark matter halo on two horizon-scale observables of a black hole: its shadow and quasinormal-mode spectrum. We consider a Schwarzschild black hole embedded in a Hernquist halo and construct a one-parameter family of solutions that preserve the total halo mass while varying how the halo density vanishes at the horizon. By closing the Einstein equations with an Einstein-cluster stress tensor, we show that horizon regularity requires the density to vanish at least linearly. Our results also indicate that the dominant energy condition is violated in a thin layer outside the horizon, highlighting the limitations of the Einstein-cluster description within the photon sphere. We demonstrate that, at fixed black hole mass, the halo always enlarges the shadow, with the effect becoming more pronounced for more massive and compact halos. Comparison with Event Horizon Telescope observations of Sgr\,A$^*$ and M87$^*$ shows that only sufficiently compact halos can be constrained, with the inferred bounds depending sensitively on whether the observed mass is identified with the black hole mass or the total mass of the system. We further show that the halo lowers both the oscillation frequencies and damping rates of electromagnetic and axial gravitational quasinormal modes, leading to higher quality factors. These spectral shifts are quantitatively explained by changes in the photon-sphere properties through the eikonal correspondence. Since the effects scale with the ratio of the halo mass to its size, they are observable only for dark matter concentrated within a few tens of gravitational radii of the black hole, which is the regime considered here.

title: Mass-Varying Dark Matter, Naturally
summary: Ultralight scalars that vary dark-matter masses require protection from quantum corrections. Cyclic $\mathbb{Z}_N$ symmetries provide this protection but also suppress variation of the mean mass of equally populated partners. Unsuppressed variation typically requires asymmetric reheating through symmetry-breaking couplings that threaten radiative control. We show that scalar-induced mass splittings built into these constructions can instead bias relic abundances through symmetric interactions. The mechanism applies to thermal and nonthermal relics that reach internal equilibrium after production, and permits mass variation over a broad range of timescales.

title: JWST observations of the planetary nebula NGC 6302 IV: PAH spectral characteristics, formation and evolution
comment: 20 pages, 8 figures, 7 tables including 6 in appendices, accepted in MNRAS
summary: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) and carbonaceous dust have been observed in Oxygen-rich planetary nebulae (PNe), yet their formation and evolution in these environments is an open question. We aim to study the formation and evolution of the PAHs in the O-rich PN NGC 6302, by characterizing the PAH emission throughout this object. We obtained JWST MIRI IFU spectroscopic observations of NGC 6302 pointed at its central source. From these, we extract four template spectra that are representative of the variation in PAH emission throughout NGC 6302. We detect the major PAH features at 6.2, 7.7, 8.6, 11.2, and 12.7 $μ$m, and several minor PAH features. The template spectra vary in terms of their PAH feature widths, peak wavelengths, and relative intensities. The 11.2 $μ$m PAH feature is class B, typical for PNe. The 6-9 $μ$m PAH features are class A, which is less common for PNe. We estimate the PAH charge to be 75% cations on average, based on the 7.7/11.2 PAH feature ratio. The relative strengths of the 11-15 $μ$m PAH features indicate a range of PAH edge structures. To ensure consistency in our observations and explain variable PAH feature widths, we propose a variation in the size of the PAHs throughout NGC 6302, and suggest variation in the shielding of these PAHs. The PAHs range from large and non-compact, to small and compact. We find that NGC 6302 formed PAHs in-situ in the current PN phase, likely from small hydrocarbons formed by the photodissociation of CO.

title: Simulation-based inference of profile evolution for high-precision pulsar timing
summary: Pulsars are exceptional cosmic laboratories, the most stable of which rival atomic clocks. Nearly all of that precision rests on one observable, the average pulse profile unique to each pulsar and stable over decades. These profiles change shape systematically with observing frequency, reflecting the physics of the emitting pulsar beam, but if left unmodelled, it can bias the arrival-time measurements, undermining precision timing. Profile-domain timing has been proposed to address this effect, but current implementations use stochastic sampling, which is computationally prohibitive and has limited the application in large-scale analyses. Here, we present a simulation-based inference approach to profile-domain timing, using a normalising flow conditioned on a convolutional embedding of the frequency-phase portrait. From a single portrait, it returns joint posteriors on dispersion measures, arrival times, and the parameters governing profile evolution instantaneously, with uncertainties verified against known inputs following an initial training run. The value of a likelihood-free approach is that the simulator becomes the interface to pulsar properties. Fundamental properties like non-Gaussian noise, pulsar self-noise, jitter, scattering, and profile change can be inferred by simulating them rather than by deriving a new likelihood for each, opening a promising pathway to include machine learning methods into pulsar timing workflows.

title: Cosmological Inference with Gravitational-Wave Dark Sirens and 21-cm Intensity Mapping: Forecasts for LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA with MeerKAT and SKAO
comment: 17 pages, 9 figures. Submitted to MNRAS. Comments are welcome
summary: Gravitational waves (GWs) and 21-cm intensity mapping (IM) are emerging as complementary cosmological probes: GWs provide direct luminosity-distance measurements, while neutral-hydrogen (HI) IM traces the matter distribution in redshift space. Their synergy offers a promising avenue for precise measurements of the Hubble constant.
